subject: Reserved capacity commit — Helix AI pricing sensitivity and approval path
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@helix.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Reserved capacity commit — Helix AI pricing sensitivity and approval path

Hi Jorge / Priya,

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. To keep momentum, I wanted to outline the ask we discussed: Helix is evaluating a 24-month reserved capacity commitment (targeting a mix of A100 and H100 equivalents) and needs visibility into how discounts would change if GPU spot-market costs or supplier prices move by +/- 20%.

Attached is a simple capacity/price model and a proposed term sheet draft. Key open items for internal review:
- Discount tiers tied to committed vCPU/GPU hours and absolute spend thresholds
- A GPU-indexation clause: what band triggers pricing re-evaluation vs. automatic pass-through
- Fallback policy (burst to hosted pool) and SLA credit mechanics in the event of capacity constraints

Can Karthik + Monica validate the operational sizing assumptions in the sheet? I’ll pull Finance into pricing sensitivity and approval once we have a recommended ask (and an explicit executive exception path if needed).

Next step: I propose we present a single option with two alternate pricing triggers (indexation vs. fixed floor) so Helix can choose with legal. Targeting a finalize-for-signature timeline: EOW 11/16 if we can get approvals.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: helix_commit_term_model.xlsx (capacity + pricing model), helix_term_sheet_draft.pdf (term sheet)
From: Jorge Alvarez <procurement@helix.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity commit — Helix AI pricing sensitivity and approval path

David,

Appreciate the follow-up and the model. A couple clarifying Qs from our procurement and finance teams:
1) For the indexation clause — can you clarify the benchmark (spot vs. list from our provider)? We need clarity on delta calculation and notification cadence.
2) If GPU costs spike >25% we will need an option to reduce committed SKUs for a 3-month window without breaking the overall commitment (a temporary step-down). Is that something Redwood can operationalize or would that require an exception?
3) We’ll want an explicit example of the discount math at three breakpoints (base / +15% / +25%) to show our CFO.

I’ve CC’d Helix legal — they will want the precise fallback language.

Thanks,
Jorge
Jorge Alvarez
Head of Procurement, Helix AI
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-13T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity commit — Helix AI pricing sensitivity and approval path

Karthik / Monica — forwarding Jorge's questions. I’ve attached the model again. Please review the sizing assumptions and confirm whether a 3-month step-down with immediate operational rebalancing is feasible (we should call out the lead time to reprovision and any potential perf degradation).

Also looping Naomi from Finance to help with the discount math and to propose an approval ladder if we need to exceed standard discount caps.

(Attachment: helix_commit_term_model.xlsx)

Thanks,
David
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-14T13:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity commit — Helix AI pricing sensitivity and approval path

Team,

I ran three scenarios off the sheet you shared (base, +15% GPU cost, +25% GPU cost). Summary:
- Standard discount bands (up to 18% total discount at the largest committed tier) hold through a +10% supplier cost movement.
- At +15% we need an executive exception to preserve the same net-of-cost discount; otherwise the effective margin drops below our 12% floor.
- At +25% we recommend either: (a) enact a pass-through increase to Helix with a 60-day notice, or (b) allow Helix a one-time contractual step-down of up to 20% of committed SKUs for a 3-month window, with a commensurate pro-rated credit and re-onboarding fees.

Recommended approval path:
1) Up to 18% discount: Sales + Finance sign-off (no exec)
2) 18%–23% discount: require Marcus' sign-off (VP Finance ops) — documented as ExecException-22
3) >23% discount or a permanent SKU reduction: require C-level approval (Marcus to escalate)

If you want, I’ll prepare a short memo with the math and an example table for Helix’s CFO. I also drafted constrained language for the indexation clause (I’ll attach).

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Commercial Finance

Attachments: pricing_matrix_v3.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity commit — Helix AI pricing sensitivity and approval path

Confirming conditional approval.

I approve an exception up to 22% aggregate discount for the HLX-2026-0923 commitment under these conditions:
- We include a GPU-cost indexation clause that uses a publicly auditable benchmark (use AWS p3/p4 list pricing regional index) and a 45-day notification window.
- Step-down option: Helix can reduce committed SKUs by up to 15% for no more than one 90-day window; any additional reductions require C-level sign-off.
- If net effective margin on the deal drops below 9% at any point, automatic re-pricing review is triggered and the deal moves to the Pricing Council.

Please update the term sheet with those bullets and share a single consolidated option set for Helix to choose from. If legal needs an exec cover note, I’ll provide one.

Marcus Lin
VP, Revenue Operations
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jorge Alvarez <procurement@helix.ai>, Priya Shah <pm@helix.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Helix AI Legal <legal@helix.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T15:08:00-08:00
Subject: Final: Helix reserved capacity options + next steps (DocuSign link)

Jorge / Priya — thanks for the questions and patience. We’ve consolidated two options into the attached term-sheet pdf:
Option A: Fixed-band discount with a 22% max discount (exec exception) + indexation floor
Option B: Lower baseline discount + explicit 90-day step-down allowance (15% max) and pass-through at >25% cost shock

Marcus has approved the conditional exception language (see CC). Naomi attached the sensitivity math. Karthik & Monica confirmed operational feasibility for the proposed step-down window.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached consolidated term-sheet and pick A or B by EOD 11/18 so we can route to your legal.
2) If you’re ready, I’ll send a DocuSign envelope with the selected option (pre-filled) — link below will be live once you confirm the option.

DocuSign: https://docusign.net/prepare/AX7-helix-term-sheet
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company.com/deal/HLX-2026-0923

Best,
David
